narrative: Population: organizer usable_for_training = 11,942 events (8,946 Safe / 2,162 Elevated / 834 Critical); our final-tier labels match the organizer file on all 13,154 events (0 mismatches on the usable set). Inputs: CDMs with ttca >= 2 d only, harness A13 (84) / ALL (233) features; on the 8,293 Kelvins events they are bit-identical to research/bakeoff features.

Sub-populations by final-message ttca: final_lt1d 8,293 (551 crit; = Kelvins-eligible set), final_1to2d 599 (39 crit), final_ge2d 3,050 (244 crit). On final_ge2d the final message IS the latest input, so persistence (latest >= 2 d tier) is exact by construction (recall 1, 0 FA, macro-F1 1). Any skill claimed on the full organizer population is diluted/inflated by this 26 % slice; the forecasting problem lives in final_lt1d and final_1to2d.

No 'is this the final message' feature (unknowable at prediction time). The models do see last_time_to_tca, which is legitimate. Test events all have their latest message at 2.0-6.9 d (median 2.19 d), i.e. they look like truncated events.

Alert cut-off: per outer fold, inner 5-fold OOF on the training part only (KFold by event for 80/20, GroupKFold by mission for the mission split); threshold = argmin 10*missed + FA subject to inner recall >= 90 %. Persistence alert = latest tier is Critical; persistence_costcut = same rule applied to the ordinal latest tier (it picks >= Elevated: recall 0.98 but ~4x the false alarms, cost/1000 ~200).

Recommended: LightGBM ALL trained on the organizer population. vs persistence it cuts R=10 cost by ~30 % on both splits (80/20: 80.1 vs 110.8; mission: 72.8 vs 104.3 per 1000 events) and raises critical recall from ~0.85-0.87 to ~0.94-0.95, at ~3.5x the false alarms. Macro-F1 of the argmax tier is a tie with persistence (persistence gets a free 1.0 on final_ge2d); on final_lt1d LightGBM is level on macro-F1 and much better on cost/recall/AUC.

Training population: organizer (11,942) beats Kelvins-only (8,293) mainly through final_ge2d (macro-F1 ~0.97 vs ~0.86, fewer FA) and better Elevated recall overall (0.85-0.87 vs 0.77-0.78); on final_lt1d the two are statistically tied (by mission: Kelvins-trained macro-F1 0.879 vs 0.870, organizer-trained cost/1000 86 vs 94; both within CI). So train on the organizer population. ALL vs A13 (both organizer-trained) is within CI on cost; ALL has the higher macro-F1 and AUC and was the bake-off winner, so ALL is kept.

Final model fitted on all 11,942; alert threshold p_critical >= 0.0634 from a by-event 5-fold OOF on the training data (OOF recall 0.954). Test (2,167 events): predicted tiers {'Safe': 1512, 'Elevated': 480, 'Critical': 175}, 287 CRITICAL alerts; persistence tiers {'Safe': 1481, 'Elevated': 500, 'Critical': 186}.

CIs: event bootstrap (B=500); for 80/20 each of the 5 seed test sets is resampled independently and the metric averaged over seeds (counts like FA are per ~2,389-event test set); for mission the pooled OOF over all 11,942 is resampled. CIs are marginal per model, not paired differences.
The cost-based sweep (research/sweep/SELECTION.md, registry/forecaster_cost/) had not produced a selection when this ran; its config is not included.
